custom_g_codes.description: Tool carrier (swivel head) kinematics selection — defines which kinematic chain to use for transformations
Feedforward ON — enables velocity feedforward for reduced following error during high-speed moves
Soft acceleration — uses jerk-limited acceleration profiles for smooth axis motion
Brisk acceleration — uses maximum axis acceleration for fastest response (sharper corners)
Orientation interpolation via rotary axes — tool orientation changes by direct A/C axis motion
Orientation interpolation via vector — tool orientation changes by interpolating the tool tip direction vector
Rigid tapping cycle — synchronizes spindle and Z axis for rigid tapping
Drilling cycle — single-pass drilling to programmed depth

Modal subroutine call — repeats subroutine at every subsequent position (for hole patterns)

Spindle stop — stops spindle rotation

Through-spindle coolant off

programming_tips.code_example:
CYCLE800(0,"TABLE_ROTARY",0,27,0,0,0,30,0,0,0,0,0,1)
; Swivel: A=30, C=0, direct absolute positioning
; Parameter 27 = direct, absolute, table rotary kinematics
G54 ; reactivate WCS after swivel
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ F_ ; mill in tilted plane
CYCLE800() ; cancel swivel, return to base position
programming_tips.description: CYCLE800 performs 3+2 coordinate system transformation. It calculates the A and C rotary axis positions to orient the table so the Z-axis of the WCS points in the desired tool direction. After CYCLE800, program normally in G54/G01 — the control handles the coordinate transformation. The swivel data is configured in the machine data (kinematics chain) and must match the physical machine setup.
gotchas: Always cancel CYCLE800 before TRAORI — they are mutually exclusive modes
CYCLE800 resets work offsets — reactivate G54 after swivel call
The 'TABLE_ROTARY' string must match the machine kinematic chain name — case sensitive
Test CYCLE800 orientations in single-block mode first to verify correct rotation direction

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: CYCLE832 — High Speed Cutting Tolerance Levels
programming_tips.code_example:
CYCLE832(0.01,112001,1) ; FINISHING: 0.01mm tolerance
CYCLE832(0.05,112001,1) ; SEMI-FINISH: 0.05mm
CYCLE832(0.1,112001,1) ; ROUGHING: 0.1mm tolerance
CYCLE832() ; cancel HSC mode
programming_tips.description: CYCLE832 configures the HSC (High Speed Cutting) tolerance and smoothing behavior. The first parameter is the contour tolerance in mm — tighter tolerance produces more accurate surfaces but reduces feed rate. The second parameter is the technology type (112001 = milling). CYCLE832 also activates FFWON (feedforward), SOFT (jerk limiting), and COMPCURV (compressor) automatically. Use 0.01mm for finishing, 0.05mm for semi-finish, 0.1mm for roughing.
gotchas: CYCLE832 with tight tolerance (<0.005mm) severely limits feed rate — actual feed may be 50% of programmed
Cancel CYCLE832 before drilling cycles — HSC mode interferes with canned cycle positioning
The compressor in CYCLE832 may change programmed points — verify critical dimensions
CYCLE832 activates G642 smooth approach mode automatically — do not also program G642

programming_tips.code_example:
TRAORI ; activate 5-axis transformation
G642 ; smooth transitions
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ A3=_ B3=_ C3=_ F_ ; tool tip + tool orientation
...
TRAFOOF ; deactivate 5-axis transformation
programming_tips.description: TRAORI activates the 5-axis kinematic transformation that maintains the tool center point (TCP) position while the rotary axes (A and C) change orientation. With TRAORI active, the control automatically compensates all linear axes to keep the tool tip at the programmed XYZ while rotating. Use A3=, B3=, C3= to specify tool orientation as a direction vector instead of axis angles. TRAORI is required for all simultaneous 5-axis contouring.
gotchas: Cancel CYCLE800 before activating TRAORI — they cannot be active simultaneously
TRAORI significantly changes axis dynamics — reduce feed rate for first test run
Tool length offset MUST be correct — TCP errors create large position errors amplified by rotation
TRAFOOF must be called before changing tool — ATC operates in machine coordinates

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: Jerk Optimization — SOFT vs BRISK vs G642
programming_tips.code_example:
SOFT ; jerk-limited acceleration — smooth, lower vibration
BRISK ; maximum acceleration — fastest response, more vibration
G642 ; continuous-path with optimized transitions between blocks
G641 ADIS=0.1 ; continuous-path with specific rounding tolerance (0.1mm)
programming_tips.description: Siemens provides three axis dynamic modes: BRISK = maximum acceleration (best cycle time but more vibration), SOFT = jerk-limited (smoother surface, less vibration), G642 = optimized continuous-path transitions. For finishing: SOFT + G642 gives best surface quality. For roughing: BRISK gives best cycle time. G641 with ADIS allows specifying exact corner rounding tolerance.
gotchas: BRISK can cause visible marks at direction reversals on finish surfaces
SOFT reduces axis acceleration by 30-50% — increases cycle time on rapid-heavy programs
G642 without CYCLE832 does not activate feedforward — combine for best results
ADIS value in G641 is the physical rounding deviation from programmed corner — too large causes dimension errors

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: ShopMill to G-Code — Conversational Program Conversion
programming_tips.description: DMU 50 with CELOS supports ShopMill conversational programming for quick job shop work. ShopMill programs can be converted to standard G-code for editing, archiving, or post-processing. From the ShopMill editor: Menu > Convert > To DIN/ISO. The converted program preserves all operations but uses CYCLE81/83/800/832 calls. Useful for operators who prefer graphical programming but need G-code output for CAM integration.
gotchas: Converted ShopMill programs are verbose — 3x larger than hand-written G-code
Some ShopMill contour operations convert to CYCLE62 which is not standard across Siemens machines
Converting back from G-code to ShopMill is not supported — one-way conversion only
ShopMill simulation does not check for 5-axis collisions — use CELOS 3D simulation instead

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.description: CELOS provides a unified app ecosystem on the 24-inch touch screen. Key apps: JOB MANAGER (organizes programs, tools, offsets per job), TOOL HANDLING (graphical tool setup), STATUS MONITOR (real-time machine monitoring), PRODUCTION PLANNER (scheduling), APPLICATION CONNECTOR (links to CAM/ERP). JOB MANAGER is especially valuable — saves complete job packages (program + tool list + offsets + setup sheet) for instant recall of repeat jobs.
gotchas: CELOS apps run alongside NC — they do not affect machining performance
JOB MANAGER packages must be updated when tool offsets change between batches
STATUS MONITOR data is available via network for remote monitoring (configure in CELOS settings)
Some CELOS apps require optional licenses — check with DMG dealer

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: COMPCAD — 3D Cutter Radius Compensation for Surface Machining
programming_tips.code_example:
COMPCAD ; activate 3D tool compensation
G41 D1 ; left side compensation with tool D1 values
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ A3=_ B3=_ C3=_ F_
...
G40 ; cancel cutter compensation
COMPOF ; deactivate 3D compensation
programming_tips.description: COMPCAD enables 3D cutter radius compensation using surface normal vectors output by the CAM system. Unlike 2D G41/G42, COMPCAD adjusts the tool position in all three axes based on the surface normal direction at each point. This allows accurate re-machining with a different tool diameter without re-posting from CAM. Essential for tool diameter fine-tuning and wear compensation on 3D surfaces.
gotchas: COMPCAD requires A3/B3/C3 surface normal vectors in the NC program — not all CAM posts output these
Tool diameter change >20% of original may cause gouging on concave surfaces
COMPCAD processing overhead reduces block processing speed — keep blocks >0.05mm for smooth motion
Combine with CYCLE832 for best surface finish results

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: Safe Program Start Block for Siemens 840D
programming_tips.code_example:
G17 G40 G49 G54 G80 G90 ; safety line
TRAFOOF ; cancel any active 5-axis transformation
CYCLE800() ; cancel any active swivel
G0 G53 Z0 D0 ; rapid Z to machine zero, no tool offset
T1 D1 M6 ; load first tool
programming_tips.description: Every Siemens 840D program should start with a comprehensive safety block that cancels all modal states. G17=XY plane, G40=cancel cutter comp, G49=cancel tool length, G54=WCS1, G80=cancel cycles, G90=absolute. Additionally, cancel TRAORI (TRAFOOF) and CYCLE800 to ensure no leftover transformations. Then safe Z retract with G53 Z0. This prevents carryover from previous programs or ShopMill operations.
gotchas: TRAFOOF and CYCLE800() cancellation are unique to 5-axis machines — do not omit
G53 Z0 D0 ensures Z moves to machine zero without any tool offset — safest retract
Include FFWOF to cancel feedforward if it may have been left active
On DMU 50, always verify A and C are at known angles before starting a new program

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: Tool Preselection for Faster Tool Changes
programming_tips.code_example:
T1 D1 M6 ; load T1
(machining with T1)
T2 ; preselect T2 in magazine during machining
...
M6 ; execute change — T2 already in position, fast swap
(machining with T2)
T3 ; preselect T3
...
programming_tips.description: On the DMU 50, the T command preselects the next tool (moves it to the magazine ready position) while the current tool is machining. The M6 command then executes the physical swap. This reduces chip-to-chip time to ~1.5 seconds because the magazine does not need to search during the tool change. Always preselect the next tool immediately after loading the current one.
gotchas: T command alone does NOT change the tool — M6 is still required
Preselection only works if the magazine has time to reach position — call T early enough
If T is called right before M6 on the same line, preselection is wasted — separate by at least one block

source.handbook_title: DMG MORI DMU 50 Operation & Programming Manual 2SL700-SA-0003E Rev B

programming_tips.topic: ORIAXES vs ORIVECT — Orientation Interpolation Modes
programming_tips.code_example:
TRAORI
ORIAXES ; tool orientation by direct A/C axis motion
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ A_ C_ F_
...
ORIVECT ; tool orientation by vector interpolation
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ A3=_ B3=_ C3=_ F_
programming_tips.description: TRAORI supports two orientation interpolation modes. ORIAXES: the control moves A and C axes directly from start to end angle — shortest axis path but tool may tilt unpredictably on long orientation changes. ORIVECT: the control interpolates the tool direction vector linearly — more predictable tool tip path but may require larger axis motions. Use ORIAXES for small angle changes (<15 deg per block). Use ORIVECT for large orientation changes and on surfaces where tool direction consistency matters.
gotchas: ORIAXES near A=0 (singularity) causes extremely fast C-axis motion — avoid
ORIVECT requires A3/B3/C3 vector output from CAM post processor
Switching between ORIAXES and ORIVECT mid-program may cause a small tool tip deviation at transition

programming_tips.description: Siemens R-parameters (R0-R299) are persistent floating-point variables available for parametric programming. Unlike Fanuc macro variables, Siemens supports structured programming with IF/ELSE/ENDIF, WHILE/ENDWHILE, REPEAT/UNTIL, FOR/ENDFOR, and CASE/ENDCASE. R-parameters survive power cycles. Use for part family programming, probing result storage, and adaptive machining logic.
gotchas: R0-R299 are global and persistent — avoid conflicts with cycle R-parameter usage (CYCLE81/83 use R-params internally)
Some cycles use specific R-parameters — check cycle documentation before using R0-R50
Siemens also supports LUD (Local User Data) and GUD (Global User Data) for more organized variable management

programming_tips.topic: Workpiece Weight Limits and Table Balance for 5-Axis
programming_tips.description: The DMU 50 swivel rotary table supports 300 kg maximum load, but practical limits depend on the center of gravity height and A-axis tilt angle. At A=0 (horizontal table), full 300 kg is allowed. At A=90 (vertical table), limit drops to ~150 kg due to overturning moment. Always calculate the moment: Weight x CG_height x sin(A_angle) must be under the table's moment capacity (450 Nm). For heavy parts, reduce A-axis rapid speed to prevent inertial overshoot.
gotchas: Eccentric workpieces create dynamic imbalance during C-axis rotation — reduce C speed for asymmetric parts
Heavy vises add to the weight budget — a 50kg vise on a 300kg table leaves only 250kg for the workpiece
Dynamic forces during rapid deceleration add to static weight — use SOFT mode for heavy parts
Always verify with table load calculator in CELOS before machining
